title: Vitamin D Deficiency: Testing Indications and Treatment

evidenceAudit.scope: Adult with suspected vitamin D deficiency: who to test, 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25(OH)D) thresholds, loading and maintenance colecalciferol, calcium advice, safety and monitoring, using the Royal Osteoporosis Society guideline.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-18.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: Only the Royal Osteoporosis Society guideline (2018, reviewed February 2020; review date December 2021 has passed) was opened; its scope excludes severe or end-stage chronic kidney disease (stages 4 to 5).
No hypercalcaemia, hyperparathyroidism or sarcoidosis list of formal contraindications is given; they are discussed under toxicity and specialist input.
Saudi-specific thresholds or Saudi Ministry of Health vitamin D guidance were not opened, and the Saudi prevalence of deficiency was not checked.
Source pages were read through automated page extraction rather than page-by-page in the original documents, so each figure should be spot-checked against the source during clinical review.
The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.

pathophysiology.summary: A plasma 25(OH)D below 25 nmol/L is deficient; 25 to 50 nmol/L may be inadequate in some people; above 50 nmol/L is sufficient for almost the whole population. Treatment is a loading regimen totalling about 300,000 IU followed by maintenance of 800 to 2,000 IU daily. Overt vitamin D toxicity manifests as chronic hypercalcaemia; the long-term upper limit is 4,000 IU daily. Calcium and vitamin D combination products should not be used as the source of vitamin D for loading regimens.

clinicalManagement.title: Test selectively
actions: Test people with musculoskeletal symptoms possibly due to deficiency or bone disease; do not screen asymptomatic populations.

clinicalManagement.title: Loading regimen
actions: Total about 300,000 IU: for example 50,000 IU weekly for 6 weeks, or 1,000 IU four times a day for 10 weeks (280,000 IU); vitamin D3 orally.

clinicalManagement.title: Maintenance
actions: 800 to 2,000 IU daily; up to 4,000 IU daily occasionally.

clinicalManagement.title: Calcium and monitoring
actions: Check adjusted calcium; promote dietary calcium; do not use calcium and vitamin D combinations for loading.

regimens.indication: Loading regimen for vitamin D deficiency
adjustments: Loading may be weekly or daily over six to ten weeks.
Scope excludes CKD stages 4 to 5; activated vitamin D preparations (calcitriol, alfacalcidol) are not recommended.
monitoring: Adjusted calcium about one month after loading.
